literary-boston-as-i-knew-it-from-litera:
William Dean Howells recalls his arrival in Boston in 1866. He came to serve as assistant editor of the Atlantic Monthly. Samuel Bowles of the Springfield Republican shared his train ride. Bowles had earlier suffered cruel insomnia from newspaper overwork.

Bowles delighted in the drama of a young Ohio newspaperman's rise. A western novice would now share the Atlantic's destinies. Howells doubts such a fact would move anyone today. The West has since flooded the East with authorship, he writes. Scarcely an hour of sleep in twenty-four marked Bowles's suffering. Venice had hosted their earlier meeting years before this train ride.
nasa-tm-19650025634-nasa-flight-research:
William E Gray Jr, head of a Flight Research Center branch at Edwards, described a handling-qualities program for small private aircraft in April 1964. He spoke at a general aviation design meeting in Wichita, Kansas. Handling qualities are how an aircraft feels and responds to its pilot. Small aircraft had rarely received the formal testing given to military types.

A set program brings test pilots and clear standards to that work. Poor handling in a light aircraft is a safety issue for ordinary owners. Gray sets out what the center's program did and why it mattered. The paper shows flight research reaching beyond rockets and jets, into everyday flying.
